entry.summary: Visa-free short stays: Luxembourg is an EU member in the Schengen area.
entry.max_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area
entry.other: Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

sources.title: Schengen area
sources.authority: European Commission, Migration and Home Affairs

meetings.detail: Business meetings are covered, without being employed in the country.

conference.detail: Business travel, including conferences, is covered.

unpaid-speaking.detail: Unpaid speaking during a business visit is generally covered; the paid-activity exclusion is read narrowly.
unpaid-speaking.next: If unsure, ask Consulate of Luxembourg (honorary).

paid-speaking.detail: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Consulate of Luxembourg (honorary).
paid-speaking.next: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Consulate of Luxembourg (honorary).

book-launch.detail: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Consulate of Luxembourg (honorary).
book-launch.next: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Consulate of Luxembourg (honorary).

ai-teaching.detail: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Consulate of Luxembourg (honorary).
ai-teaching.next: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Consulate of Luxembourg (honorary).

remote-work.detail: Remote work for an employer outside the EU isn't addressed in the EU guidance read.

entrepreneur.detail: Exploring and meeting fit a business visit; running a business needs national permission.

trade.detail: Business visits are covered; selling or delivering services may be paid activity.
trade.next: Keep the trip to meetings and negotiation.

artist.detail: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Consulate of Luxembourg (honorary).
artist.next: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Consulate of Luxembourg (honorary).

mixed-mission.detail: The visa-free stay covers the business and tourism parts; any paid part needs national permission.

filming.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (journalistic or media purposes)
filming.detail: Journalistic or media purposes are listed among visa-free purposes; paid production work and location permits are national matters.
filming.next: Ask the Consulate of Luxembourg (honorary) about filming, and the local authority about locations.

research.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (short-term study or training)
research.detail: Short-term study and training are covered; paid research at an institution is paid activity.
research.next: Ask the Consulate of Luxembourg (honorary) if the host pays you.

volunteering.detail: Volunteering isn't addressed in the EU guidance read.

sources.title: Frequently asked questions on the Schengen visa-free regime
sources.supports: visa-free stays cover business meetings, journalistic or media purposes, short-term study or training; paid activity is excluded and needs national permission
